_note: Bajaj Finance (consolidated, incl. Bajaj Housing Finance) lender model, as of 30-Sep-2026 on a Q1FY27 basis. Sources: Q1FY27 presentation (30-Jul-2026) and call; Q4FY26 presentation (29-Apr-2026, FY27 'management assessment'); Q4FY23-Q4FY25 presentations for history; Screener.in for the statements. Equity raise noticed on 24-Sep-2026 is NOT in the base case (size and price unknown on 30-Sep); see the valuation chapter for its effect.

history._why: Screener-consistent history. aum = consolidated closing AUM (FY22-FY26 exact from the Q4 presentations; FY18-FY21 from the 19-year snapshot in ₹'000 cr, so rounded to ₹100 cr). provisions = loan losses and provisions on the basis Screener uses for that year: FY18-FY24 before the Q4FY26 presentation change (recoveries of written-off loans shown in income), FY25-FY26 after it (recoveries netted in provisions). feeIncome = all non-interest operating income on the same basis (FY22 'fees, commission and other non-interest income'; FY23-FY24 fees + fair-value gains + sale of services + others; FY25-FY26 non-interest income). Each basis ties to Screener revenue within ₹20 cr.

src.FY25: Q1FY27 presentation p37; Q4FY25 presentation p45
src.FY18-FY21: Q1FY27 presentation p26 (19-year snapshot, before presentation changes)

_aumGrowthWhy: FY27 management assessment (29-Apr-2026): 22-24%; long-term corridor 23-25%. Q1FY27 grew 24% with a record ₹36,969 cr added in one quarter, MSME back to growth from Q3 and gold loans to ₹29-31k cr by Mar-27 (call, 30-Jul-2026). We take the top of FY27 guidance, then fade 1pp a year as the book passes ₹8 lakh cr; FY26 itself fell short of its 24-25% guide (22%).
_yieldOnAumWhy: Interest income ÷ average AUM: 16.4% FY25, 15.7% FY26, 15.5% annualised in Q1FY27. Management guides a 10-15bp NIM moderation in FY27; the mix keeps shifting to lower-yield gold, mortgages and loans against securities; the RBI's draft ban on revolving credit for NBFCs (6-Aug-2026) puts ~50bp of extra yield on the ~14% flexi book at risk (Jefferies). We take ~15-20bp off each year.
_feeIncomePctWhy: Non-interest income ÷ average AUM: 2.06% FY25, 1.99% FY26, 2.0% in Q1FY27. Guidance: non-interest income +16-18% in FY27 vs AUM +22-24%, so the ratio drifts down.
_costOfFundsWhy: Interest expense ÷ average Screener borrowings (incl. deposits): 7.64% FY25, 7.26% FY26 (the company's own measure: 7.97% and 7.54%). Reported cost of funds was 7.40% in Q1FY27, 14bp below FY26; management expects it 'range bound with a slight upward bias' as incremental funding is 30-60bp dearer (call, 30-Jul-2026).
_opexPctWhy: Operating expenses incl. depreciation ÷ average AUM: 3.99% FY25, 3.78% FY26. Guidance: opex to net total income 25-40bp better in FY27 despite gold-loan/MFI branch openings and the Labour Codes; AI-led productivity. These values give a cost-to-income ratio of ~32.7% in FY27E (33.0% on our FY26 basis) falling ~30bp a year.
_creditCostWhy: Provisions ÷ average AUM: 1.90% FY25, 2.05% FY26 (incl. a ₹1,406 cr accelerated ECL charge). FY27 guidance 1.45-1.60% of average AUF; Q1FY27 1.54% incl. a ₹296 cr overlay (1.31% without). 1.50% of AUM ≈ 1.53% of AUF: mid-guidance, keeping room for further overlays. FY29E edges up as a normal cycle: FY23-FY26 ranged 0.96-2.09% (company basis).
_payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹6.00 per share incl. a ₹0.60 special from the BHFL stake sale (19.6% of EPS); ex-special 17.7%. FY24-FY25 payout 15-16%.
_minorityPctWhy: Minority interest in Bajaj Housing Finance. FY26 ₹315 cr (1.6% of PAT) at an 86.7-88.75% stake. Management will cut the stake to 75% (public-float rule), 'first protocol' before any capital raise (call, 30-Jul-2026). We assume two tranches (H2FY27, H1FY28), BHFL profit +21%/+21%/+20% (Q1FY27 +23%, AUM +24%): minority ₹0.46k / 0.88k / 1.13k cr.
_otherIncomeWhy: Screener 'other income' outside operations: ₹19-33 cr a year before exceptional items (FY24-FY26); FY26 included a ₹284 cr Labour Code charge.
_capitalRaiseWhy: Not new shares: the parent's equity gain from selling ~11.7% of BHFL down to 75% (5.85% each in H2FY27 and H1FY28) at ₹82 (30-Sep-2026 close), less ~14.6% tax on the gain (BFL cost ~₹12.2 a share) and less the minority interest created at book. Consolidated accounts book this in equity, not profit (as in FY26).

valuation._why: Ke = 6.5% + 1.1 × 6% = 13.1% (house rf and ERP; beta 1.1 for a large, rate- and credit-sensitive lender). sustainableRoe 20% = middle of the company's long-term 19-21% corridor. g = 10% long-run book growth in the justified P/B (about nominal GDP; below the 15-16% the franchise can fund today). Residual income fades ROE to 20% over 8 years, payout rising to 30%, 6% terminal growth.

methods.name: Justified P/B
methods.why: (ROE − g) ÷ (Ke − g) = (20 − 10) ÷ (13.1 − 10) on book at the 12-month target date.

methods.name: Residual income
methods.why: Book plus the present value of profit above the 13.1% cost of equity, ROE fading to 20%, rolled forward 6 months.
